image.alt: Midori, Samael, Kubo, and YHWH at Natasha Harbor at dawn

paragraphs: 那場戰鬥後，龍恩消失了。
日光逐漸照耀在重生的娜塔夏港。冒險者們在羅賓遜主教的引導下，回到舊教堂休息。一整晚激烈的遭遇，不論是肉體或精神上，對大家來說都太過疲憊。
儘管身受重傷，米多莉依然攙扶著好不容易重新回到他懷裡的小雪，而波則撐著身體，試圖協助米多莉。就算經歷了這一些，他依然無法全心全意地相信小雪，遑論支持他。
對於龍恩的再度消失，YHWH 表露出混雜著不滿與早已知曉的神情。在龍恩負不起茜卓博士的死亡之後，YHWH 早已放棄對他的信心。
薩梅爾緊緊將酷爆摟在懷中。在這場戰鬥中，他險些失去牠。縱使本來就已對酷爆百般照顧與疼愛，這次的事件，再一次的讓薩梅爾意識到這頭已經不小的狼，早已是他的全世界。
喜利則突然意識到一件事：若那隻名為「莫吉斯」，在墨奎斯咖啡廳蹭人的好奇小貓，就是那被稱為「狐狸」的線人......當時牠對他的背包感到好奇，似乎也說得通了。大河之心當時可正躺在他的背包內啊！但此刻，那些都已成歷史。莫吉斯已消逝，魂、骨與血也隨之消失。
問題是，當時大學城的城主沙蘭給的線索，似乎就這麼斷了。那他們該怎麼找到聖津菈大教堂地下室的傳送陣，到尖頂寺去呢？眼看身邊的伙伴都早已累壞，沒有討論的精力，喜利也認同休息一下，等清醒一點再來想辦法較好。
有如大夢初醒，龍恩再次睜開雙眼時，眼前的景象令他感到意外，卻也有點意思。那是他自從有記憶以來，最接近家的地方：尖頂寺。

從正門的位置往左邊繞過去，那藏在陰影下的繩梯儘管年久失修，但還能撐住龍恩的身軀。天還未亮，要進入尖頂寺內，還是低調些好。看著今晚守著寺廟大門的弟兄，龍恩也曾負責過那樣的崗位：既是鍛鍊年輕武僧專注與體力的好法子，也是保護全廟弟兄的必要手段。龍恩還沒離開尖頂寺前，從未聽過有誰闖入，也不知道是運氣好沒遇到什麼劫難，還是守門的弟兄真的發揮了他們的功效。這時，他想起前輩塔爾莫曾說過的「尖頂寺是全卓尼森帝國最頂尖的寺，也是最安全的堡壘。」語音剛落，便帶著他爬上那條搖搖晃晃的繩梯，就這樣偷偷從寺外溜回來，誰也沒發現。至少年幼的龍恩是這樣認為的。

龍恩撐起軀體，爬上二樓的陽台，顯得有些吃力，甚至眼角乾澀。那巫妖的手臂與那本神秘的書，理應讓他更有力氣才對，怎麼這就累了呢？莫非解開金鍊打倒那名強大的傢伙這麼費力？不懂，魔法真奇怪。龍恩決定不多想，想了也頭痛。找個安穩的地方盤腿休息比較實在。再往內走不久，有個拐彎拐進去，附近有個長年沒用的倉庫，似乎是個好選擇。年幼的龍恩有時會躲在這裡思考，想著想著就睡著，但還好他總是在被發現前溜出來。如果現在還沒有人佔走他的秘密基地，他大可以在這裡度過這一夜，然後再想想下一步該做什麼。說實在，來到尖頂寺並非他的本意，但對於這神奇的傳送能力，龍恩尚未掌握清楚。那時候似乎下意識的就傳到這裡來了。
那是來自家鄉的呼喚。
YHWH 醒來時，其他冒險者們都已盥洗完畢。羅賓遜主教捎來消息，邀請冒險者們一同到舊教堂的餐廳用餐。此刻已近中午，儘管睡了不少時間，有些傷痕還無法這麼快治癒。YHWH 看見波用著奇怪的神情看著他，他試圖對波笑一笑表示善意，卻只得到波更厭惡的表情。這小女孩(現在還用小女孩稱呼她，真的適當嗎？)在想什麼，還真摸不清頭緒。
冒險者們與小雪一併走到了餐廳。看著瑪莉修女端著盤子忙進忙出，波對於自己先前對她的敵意感到有些抱歉。現在她清楚瑪莉與「狐狸」一點關係也沒有---當然，撇除瑪莉有著狐狸的耳多外。對於自己這樣以貌取人的態度，她感到......慚愧？這感受對她而言十分陌生與新奇，是她這輩子相對少體會的概念。
在羅賓遜主教的歡迎下，冒險者們一一入座。前一晚前來營救的夥伴們也坐在桌邊。澤克一改之前誇張的穿著，以一身緊繃的西裝覆體，意外地顯得紳士；瑪琳船長和過往一樣一派輕鬆，這樣的場面，她大概也看多了；華生則依然顯得謹慎與小心，露出的微笑僵硬而制式化。不久後，瑪莉修女與其他幾名在此幫忙的修女也入座。
「不好意思，在各位開動前，我想說說幾句話。」大家的視角轉向羅賓遜主教。「首先，我想謝謝這群冒險者們。已故的湯普生爵士，一直都是教會的死敵。我聽說了昨晚發生的事，儘管過程艱辛，你們依然為教會做了很大的貢獻。你們永遠是津菈可靠的助力。」
「小雪女士。」羅賓遜主教看向縮在米多莉身旁的小雪。她因不知如何面對這一切，在餐桌上抬不起頭。「我誠心希望，我們可以將過去湯普生爵士的事留在過去就好。若您賞臉，聖津菈大教堂永遠歡迎您。」
「最後，米多莉。」羅賓遜主教露出了些許尷尬的表情，但聲音控制地理性與得體。「聖津菈大教堂歡迎你回來。這裡是妳的家，永遠都是妳的家。」
米多莉點點頭，大家便在主教的邀請下開始用餐。餐宴上，瑪琳船長大聲分享著過往冒險的故事，其中，多年前她受封爵士的那場冒險，在她口中有如神話，華麗而荒唐，卻又有幾分真實性。
想起昨天睡前的疑惑，喜利向主教提了問，希望能獲得些許協助。主教承諾開放讓他們能在聖津菈大教堂各處自由移動，不受拘束，唯有一個條件：瑪莉修女必須跟在身旁。對此，波出乎意料地率先表示感謝，認為有瑪莉修女，可以減少大家在大教堂內迷路與碰壁的機會。
午宴結束後，冒險者們協助修女們收拾環境。不久後，船隻已在港口等待冒險者了。羅賓遜主教帶著冒險者們、小雪與瑪利修女準備登船，澤克與華生則踏上瑪琳船長的船，準備出航。
「主教大人，對不起。」小雪低著頭說道。「我......我......我覺得我應該留下來，留在娜塔莎港。」
「小雪女士，您確定嗎？聖津菈大教堂可以提供您更舒服的環境，您不妨考慮一下。」羅賓遜主教再次提出善意的邀請。
「對不起。湯普生爵士的那些糟糕事，很多都是藉我的手而做的。我無法就這樣當作什麼事都沒有地瀟灑離開。」幾滴淚默默從小雪的臉頰滑落。「我得待在這裡贖罪......就算不當贖罪，我也得在這裡把爵士的宅邸打掃乾淨，不能讓誰都能闖進來。我可以繼續在那裡當個侍女，誰來當主人都無所謂，雖然......如果可以的話......」
「小雪女士，請您別介意，如果是我可以幫上忙的話，我很樂意達成您的心願。」
「是否能將娜塔莎港封給米多莉，我可以一輩子侍奉她？」小雪將頭微微轉向米多莉。「米多莉......妳願意陪我留下來嗎？」
After that battle, Ron disappeared.

Sunlight gradually spread over the reborn Natasha Harbor. Under Bishop Robinson's guidance, the adventurers returned to the old church to rest. After an entire night of fierce encounters, everyone was exhausted, in body and in spirit.

Despite her severe injuries, Midori continued to support Yuki, who had finally returned to her arms. Beau braced herself and tried to help Midori. Even after everything they had been through, she still could not bring herself to trust Yuki completely, much less stand behind her.

At Ron's disappearance once again, YHWH wore an expression that mixed displeasure with a sense that he had known it all along. When Ron had failed to take responsibility for Dr. Chandra's death, YHWH had already lost faith in him.

Samael held Kubo tightly in his arms. He had nearly lost the wolf in the battle. Though he had always showered Kubo with care and affection, this ordeal reminded Samael once more that the wolf, no longer so small, had long since become his whole world.

Siri suddenly realized something: if the curious little cat named Mogis, who had rubbed against people at Mogis Cafe, was the informant known as the Fox... then its interest in his backpack made sense. The Heart of the Great River had been inside it at the time! But all of that was history now. Mogis was gone, and the Soul, Bone, and Blood had vanished with him.

The problem was that the lead Shalan, the ruler of Great Citadel, had given them seemed to have reached a dead end. How were they supposed to find the teleportation circle in the basement of Saint Keinra Cathedral and reach Spire Temple now? Seeing that his companions were far too exhausted to discuss it, Siri agreed that it would be better to rest and think of a way forward once their minds were clearer.

When Ron opened his eyes again, as though waking from a long dream, the sight before him was surprising—and rather intriguing. It was the closest thing to home he had known for as long as he could remember: Spire Temple.

Around to the left of the main entrance, a rope ladder hung in the shadows. Though long neglected, it could still bear Ron's weight. Dawn had yet to break; if he wanted to enter the temple, it would be best to keep a low profile. Watching the brothers guarding the gates that night, Ron remembered taking that same watch himself. It was both a way to train young monks' focus and endurance and a necessary measure to protect everyone inside. Before leaving Spire Temple, Ron had never heard of anyone breaking in. He did not know whether they had simply been lucky enough to avoid trouble or whether the gatekeepers truly deserved the credit. He remembered his senior, Tarmo, once saying, “Spire Temple is the finest temple in the entire Tronison Empire, and its safest fortress.” Barely had the words left his mouth before he led Ron up that swaying rope ladder, sneaking back in from outside without anyone noticing. At least, that was what young Ron had believed.

Ron hauled himself up onto the second-floor balcony, finding the climb surprisingly difficult. Even the corners of his eyes felt dry. The lich's arm and that mysterious book should have made him stronger. Why was he tired already? Had unfastening the golden chain and defeating that powerful foe taken so much out of him? He did not understand. Magic was strange. Ron decided not to dwell on it; thinking only gave him a headache. Finding somewhere quiet to sit cross-legged and rest would be more practical. A little farther inside, around a corner, was a storeroom that had gone unused for years. It seemed a good choice. As a child, Ron sometimes hid there to think, only to fall asleep—but he had always managed to slip out before anyone found him. If no one had taken over his secret hideaway, he could spend the night there and decide what to do next afterward. In truth, he had not intended to come to Spire Temple. He still did not fully understand this miraculous power of teleportation. At the time, he seemed to have brought himself here without thinking.
It was the call of home.

By the time YHWH woke, the other adventurers had already washed and dressed. Bishop Robinson sent word inviting them to dine in the old church's dining hall. It was nearly noon. Despite the hours of sleep, some wounds would not heal so quickly. YHWH noticed Beau looking at him with a strange expression. He tried to offer a friendly smile, only to receive an even more disgusted look in return. What was going on in that little girl's head—was it even appropriate to call her a little girl anymore?—remained a mystery to him.

The adventurers went to the dining hall with Yuki. Watching Sister Mari hurry back and forth with plates, Beau felt a little sorry for her earlier hostility. She now knew that Mari had nothing to do with the Fox—apart from having fox ears, of course. The thought that she had judged someone by appearances made her feel... ashamed? It was an unfamiliar and novel feeling, one she had experienced relatively little in her life.

At Bishop Robinson's welcome, the adventurers took their seats. The companions who had come to their rescue the previous night were already at the table. Zek had exchanged his earlier flamboyant outfit for a snug-fitting suit and looked surprisingly gentlemanly. Captain Marin was as relaxed as ever; she had probably seen plenty of occasions like this. Watson remained cautious and guarded, her smile stiff and formal. Before long, Sister Mari and several other sisters helping at the church joined them.

“Forgive me, but before everyone begins, I would like to say a few words.” All eyes turned to Bishop Robinson. “First, I wish to thank our adventurers. The late Syr Thompson was always a bitter enemy of the Church. I have heard what happened last night. Despite all the hardships you faced, you have done a great service for us. You will always be trusted allies of Keinra.”

“Lady Yuki.” Bishop Robinson turned to Yuki, who was huddled beside Midori, unable to lift her head at the table because she did not know how to face any of this. “I sincerely hope we can leave the matter of Syr Thompson in the past. If you would do us the honor, Saint Keinra Cathedral will always welcome you.”

“Finally, Midori.” A trace of awkwardness crossed Bishop Robinson's face, but his voice remained measured and composed. “Saint Keinra Cathedral welcomes you back. This is your home. It will always be your home.”

Midori nodded, and at the bishop's invitation, everyone began to eat. Over the meal, Captain Marin loudly recounted tales of her past adventures. The expedition that had earned her a knighthood years ago sounded almost mythical in her telling: magnificent and outlandish, yet carrying a certain ring of truth.

Remembering the question that had troubled him before sleep, Siri asked the bishop for help. The bishop promised that they could move freely throughout Saint Keinra Cathedral, without restriction, on one condition: Sister Mari must accompany them. Unexpectedly, Beau was the first to thank him, saying that having Mari with them would reduce the chances of getting lost or running into obstacles inside the cathedral.

After lunch, the adventurers helped the sisters tidy up. Before long, a boat was waiting for them at the harbor. Bishop Robinson led the adventurers, Yuki, and Sister Mari toward it, while Zek and Watson boarded Captain Marin's ship and prepared to set sail.
“Your Grace, I'm sorry,” Yuki said with her head bowed. “I... I... I think I should stay. Here in Natasha Harbor.”
“Lady Yuki, are you certain? Saint Keinra Cathedral can offer you more comfortable surroundings. Please do consider it.” Bishop Robinson extended his kind invitation once more.

“I'm sorry. So many of the terrible things Syr Thompson did were carried out through my hands. I can't simply walk away as though nothing happened.” A few tears slipped silently down Yuki's cheeks. “I have to stay here and atone... And even if it isn't about atonement, I need to clean up his manor and make sure people can't just wander in. I can keep serving there as a maid. I don't mind who becomes its master, though... if it were possible...”
“Lady Yuki, please don't hesitate. If there is something I can do to help, I would be happy to fulfill your wish.”
“Could you grant Natasha Harbor to Midori, so that I might serve her for the rest of my life?” Yuki turned her head slightly toward Midori. “Midori... would you stay here with me?”
